cases.migration_note: Both v2 and the public Object Query route use page size bounds 1-99. Rename page_size to pageSize; a value from 1 to 99 carries over unchanged, and a literal outside 1 to 99 is clamped to the nearest bound and reported. An invalid cursor returns 500 instead of 400 on the public route (observed). The v1 route uses offset paging; update the paging logic if using v1.
cases.v1_rest: 400, body { processId, requestId, reasons[], success }; the v1 billing-documents operation uses page/pageSize offset paging, not cursor paging.
cases.v2: 400, type bad_request, errors[0].parameter page_size; raised by request-schema validation when page_size is outside 1-99 or the cursor is malformed

cases.migration_note: v2 does not return 400 for non-hex ID values in list filter parameters; the list returns no matching rows. The public route behaves the same way for identifier filters. No error-handling change is needed.
cases.v2: v2 list filters do not validate identifier format; the filter parser rejects only invalid filter syntax and invalid enum values, not non-hex ID values; a filter with a non-hex ID value is passed through and returns an empty data array.

cases.migration_note: The public Object Query route returns 400 for a missing token and 401 for an invalid token, not always 401 as v2 did. Ensure your OAuth bearer token is present and valid, and that the requesting user has permission to read invoices.
cases.v1_rest: 401 for missing or invalid credentials; 403, body { code: integer, message: string } for permission errors.
cases.v2: 401, type unauthorized, empty errors array when the bearer token is missing or invalid.

For each row of `documents[]` in the successful JSON response (keep only the invoice rows), build the `custom_fields` object. Always build the object: it is `{}` when the row has no custom fields. Use the `customFields` array when the row has one, otherwise the `custom_fields` array; turn each `{key, value, type}` entry into `key: value` (when a key appears more than once, the last entry wins). Then convert `long` and `number` values to numbers, convert `boolean` values to true or false, and leave other types unchanged; null values stay null. If the row has neither array, collect every property whose name ends in `__c` into the object; an empty array gives `{}` and the `__c` properties are then not used. Include `custom_fields` only when it was requested.
